## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The fully realised form of the Wáng-Hán *yìlǐ* commentary canon: the early-Táng imperial *zhèngyì* 正義 ("Correct Meaning") subcommentary on [王弼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%BC%BC) Wáng Bì + [韓康伯](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%9F%93%E5%BA%B7%E4%BC%AF) Hán Kāngbó's *Zhōuyì zhù* ([KR1a0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0006)), supplemented in the present recension by [陸德明](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E5%BE%B7%E6%98%8E) Lù Démíng's *Zhōuyì yīnyì* 周易音義 (the *Yì* portion of his *Jīngdiǎn shìwén* 經典釋文) and by the *Zhōuyì lüèlì* 周易略例 of Wáng Bì with [邢璹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%82%A2%E7%92%B9) Xíng Shù's Táng commentary, plus a Sìkù-period *kǎozhèng* 考證 apparatus by [朱良裘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E8%89%AF%E8%A3%98) Zhū Liángqiú, [陳浩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E6%B5%A9) Chén Hào, and [李清植](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E6%B8%85%E6%A4%8D) Lǐ Qīngzhí appended at the end of each *juàn*. Through this textus the *Yì* circulated as one of the core *Wǔ jīng zhèngyì* 五經正義 (compiled 642, revised 651–653, promulgated 653) and ultimately as the *Yì* of the *Shísān jīng zhùshū* 十三經注疏 corpus.

The Sìkù version filed here in thirteen *juàn* combines the standard ten-*juàn* *Yì zhùshū*, the one-*juàn* *Lüèlì* with Xíng Shù's commentary, the *yīnyì*, and the *kǎozhèng* layers; the original *zhèngyì* preface gave fourteen *juàn*, the *Xīn Tángshū* gives eighteen, [陳振孫](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E6%8C%AF%E5%AD%AB) Chén Zhènsūn's *Shūlù jiětí* gives thirteen, and the present ten-*juàn* main run aligns with the Wáng-Hán *zhù* reformatted *juàn* division — almost certainly a posthumous editorial unification.

The composition window 638–653 covers the Táng *zhèngyì* commission proper: notBefore the standard date for the start of the *Wǔ jīng zhèngyì* commission under [太宗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%AA%E5%AE%97) Tàizōng (Zhēnguān 12), notAfter the formal promulgation under [高宗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%AB%98%E5%AE%97) Gāozōng (Yǒnghuī 4); the underlying Wáng-Hán *zhù* layer is older (covered in [KR1a0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0006)'s 240–380 window) and the appended *kǎozhèng* is later (Qiánlóng era).

**Abstract**

[孔穎達](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%94%E7%A9%8E%E9%81%94) Kǒng Yǐngdá (574–648), of Héngshuǐ 衡水 (modern Héběi), was the leading Confucian classicist of the early Táng court and Director of the Imperial Academy (*Guózǐ jìjiǔ* 國子祭酒). Under imperial commission from [太宗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%AA%E5%AE%97) Tàizōng he led the editorial commission that produced the *Wǔ jīng zhèngyì* 五經正義 — official imperial subcommentaries on the *Yì*, *Shū*, *Shī*, *Lǐjì*, and *Zuǒ zhuàn* — first compiled in 642 (Zhēnguān 16), revised after [顏師古](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A1%8F%E5%B8%AB%E5%8F%A4) Yán Shīgǔ's critiques, and finally promulgated in 653 (Yǒnghuī 4) under [高宗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%AB%98%E5%AE%97) Gāozōng. The *Zhèngyì* set determined the imperial-examination orthodoxy on the Five Classics for the rest of the dynasty and was inherited as the canonical sub-commentary in the Sòng *Shísān jīng zhùshū* tradition.

For the *Yì*, Kǒng's commission selected [王弼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%BC%BC) Wáng Bì–[韓康伯](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%9F%93%E5%BA%B7%E4%BC%AF) Hán Kāngbó's *Zhōuyì zhù* ([KR1a0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0006)) as the canonical-note layer (against [鄭玄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%84%AD%E7%8E%84) Zhèng Xuán's [KR1a0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0003) / [KR1a0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0004) line) and produced a sub-commentary that systematically expounds it. The *Suíshū jīngjí zhì*, written under [長孫無忌](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%95%B7%E5%AD%AB%E7%84%A1%E5%BF%8C) Cháng Sūn Wújì and others *after* the *zhèngyì* was already promulgated, consequently records that "Zhèng's school is now virtually extinct" — a state of affairs the *zhèngyì* itself was instrumental in producing. The Sìkù *tiyao* delivers a measured and unusually critical assessment: the editors document, with case-by-case examples from *Fù* 復, *Qián* 9-2, *Dàguò* 9-3 *Xiàng*, *Wényán* on *Kūn* 6-5, *Shuōguà*, and other passages, that Kǒng's exposition "manifestly takes Wáng's part" and that, where Wáng's note has swept away the older Hàn glosses, the *zhèngyì* therefore lacks the usual *zhèngyì* practice of source-citation and falls back on "empty formula" (*kōng yán* 空言).

The present ten-*juàn* recension combines the *zhù* and the *shū* — the standard *zhùshū* 注疏 textus that became canonical in the late Táng and Sòng. The Sìkù WYG print augments this with [陸德明](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E5%BE%B7%E6%98%8E) Lù Démíng's *yīnyì*, [邢璹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%82%A2%E7%92%B9) Xíng Shù's commentary on the *Lüèlì*, and a *kǎozhèng* apparatus by [朱良裘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E8%89%AF%E8%A3%98) Zhū Liángqiú, [陳浩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E6%B5%A9) Chén Hào, and [李清植](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E6%B8%85%E6%A4%8D) Lǐ Qīngzhí (compiled in connection with [Qiánlóng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%AB%98%E5%AE%97%E5%BC%98%E6%9B%86)'s 1747 imperial reissue of the *Shísān jīng* set, whose preface stands at the head of the Kanripo source file). The *Lǚ Lán* 呂蘭 collation by [阮元](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%98%AE%E5%85%83) Ruǎn Yuán (1815) is a later, fuller textual recension, supplementing this Sìkù base.

The work is the canonical "second layer" of *Yì* commentary — the lens through which the imperially-orthodox *Yì* was read from the late seventh century through the end of the imperial era — and one of the foundational documents of medieval Chinese exegetical practice.
